question: The tetracyclines act on the:

options.opb: Transpeptidation of the peptidoglycan in the wall.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Tetracyclines -> bind to the 30S subunit of the ribosome -> inhibit protein synthesis -> 95% confidence. CHAIN: Tetracyclines -> disrupt the attachment of aminoacyl-tRNA to the A site of the ribosome -> prevent elongation of the polypeptide chain -> 95%
analysis: Tetracyclines are a class of antibiotics that inhibit protein synthesis in bacteria by binding to the 30S subunit of the ribosome, thereby preventing the attachment of aminoacyl-tRNA to the mRNA-ribosome complex.
